report.headline: EuroLeague playmaker projected for a near-average NBA usage role, but the shooting projection is not trustworthy

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to fall to 19.4% in the NBA from 24.4% in the EuroLeague, landing almost exactly at the NBA average of 20.1% (sd 5.2%). This projection is informative: the model's mean absolute error of 3.3% beats the trivial league-mean baseline's 4.3% on this metric, though the 80% interval (14.2% to 24.7%) still spans roughly two NBA standard deviations.

risks.text: Turnover rate was elevated at 18.6% in the EuroLeague, a concern for ball-handling responsibility even in a reduced NBA role.

True shooting was already below the EuroLeague average (53.7%, -0.55 sd), and the NBA projection of 53.0% carries no real information because the model's error (4.7%) matches the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7%) on this metric.
Even the central usage projection (19.4%) sits below the NBA average (20.1%), and the 95% interval extends down to 11.4%, leaving meaningful downside risk to his on-court role.

strengths.text: Heavy involvement as a passer in the EuroLeague, posting 7.058 assists per 75 possessions and a 32.5% assist rate.

Usage sat well above the EuroLeague average (+0.96 sd) at 24.4%, indicating a genuinely ball-dominant role rather than a marginal one, and the model still projects him to retain a usage share near the NBA average (19.4%, 80% interval 14.2%-24.7%).

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate, 14.2% to 24.7%, covers about two standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution (sd 5.2%), so the model can rank this player against peers but not pin down his exact role. The true shooting projection of 53.0% should not be read as informative at all: the model's error there (4.7%) is no better than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7%), meaning it loses to simply guessing the league average.
